source.title: Imitating Deep Learning Dynamics via Locally Elastic Stochastic Differential Equations
source.authors: Jiayao Zhang; Hua Wang; Weijie Su

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes feature separability as a route to vanishing training loss and compares modeled feature dynamics with neural network training; its experiments do not directly measure CIFAR training classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper's main result is a theoretical phase transition in separability under its LE-SDE assumptions. The CIFAR experiment reports validation accuracy, not training classification error. Label-corruption results are on Geo MNIST, not CIFAR. The paper cites prior work on local elasticity and neural collapse; those cited results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures feature dynamics and separability, reports CIFAR validation accuracy, and reports vanishing training loss only on synthetic Geo MNIST. None measures the CIFAR training-error outcome in V1 or the comparisons specified in V2–V6. Its LE-SDE separability theorems concern a surrogate process rather than gradient training of the networks named in the versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate, but needs qualification: the authors derive separability transitions under their LE-SDE assumptions, including conditions on local-elasticity strength and decay rate, and predict neural collapse under additional conditions. They conclude that the L-model can approximate measured neural-network logit dynamics using estimated elasticity strengths. Simulated trajectories are rescaled to match convergence magnitudes, and trajectories for incorrect classes can remain mismatched.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes and analyzes LE-SDE/ODE models of feature dynamics and compares them with neural network experiments; it does not reproduce the original training-error measurements in V1.
record.method_sensitivity: Label corruption ratio: the text reports a separability transition around perr≈2/3 on Geo MNIST. The estimated local-elasticity tail behavior also varies with label corruption.

fits_no_version.finding: AlexNet variants achieve validation accuracy above 90% on two- or three-class CIFAR subsets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Convolutional networks achieve high held-out accuracy on restricted CIFAR classification tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: AlexNet variants are reported to reach zero training and validation cross-entropy loss on Geo MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient training can achieve vanishing training loss on synthetic geometric-shape classification.

fits_no_version.finding: Validation outcomes suggest failure of class separation near or above 2/3 label corruption on Geo MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label corruption can disrupt held-out class separation on synthetic geometric-shape classification.

fits_no_version.finding: The LE-SDE model predicts asymptotic feature separation under sufficiently persistent local elasticity and non-separation when that effect decays too quickly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the specified stochastic feature model, local-elasticity strength and its decay rate govern asymptotic separability.

record.problems: CIFAR evidence is reported as validation accuracy, not training classification error. The CIFAR experiments use only K∈[2,3] classes. Label-corruption results are on synthetic Geo MNIST. Several plotted results are described qualitatively without tabulated values; estimated local-elasticity quantities depend on numerical differentiation and filter window choices.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible findings were omitted. The paper's theoretical separability results describe its LE-SDE model rather than an independently measured neural network outcome.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels; dependence on model size, early stopping, or regularization.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks.
Training degradation with depth and comparisons involving identity shortcuts, special tanh initializations, or Fixup.
Effects of initialization on learning speed, signal propagation, or trainable depth.
Loss recovery, curvature evolution, or divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both extracted limits_scope verdicts: missing measurements and an out-of-scope dataset are untested components, not evidence limiting V1. No additional result in the supplied text directly tests a supplied version.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100; zero or near-zero CIFAR training classification error; random labels on CIFAR; comparisons with smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes. The CIFAR experiment uses K∈[2,3] and reports validation accuracy rather than training classification error.

rows.subject: variants of the ALEXNET model
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with K∈[2,3] classes under softmax cross-entropy; the paper reports validation accuracy.
rows.note: This is a validation accuracy result, so it does not establish the V1 claim about training classification error.
rows.check: The reported CIFAR validation accuracy above 90% is accurate, but cannot establish zero or near-zero training classification error. Remove its V1 link.

rows.subject: variants of the ALEXNET model
rows.operation_detail: Trained on Geo MNIST with softmax cross-entropy; training and validation losses are reported to converge to zero.
rows.note: The dataset is synthetic rather than CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100.
rows.check: Zero training and validation loss is reported on Geo MNIST, outside V1's CIFAR scope. The statement in Section 4.1 should not be generalized to all corrupted-label conditions. The observed loss convergence is real, but does not determine any supplied version.

rows.subject: variants of the ALEXNET model
rows.operation_detail: Trained on Geo MNIST with varying label pollution ratio; validation loss and accuracy are plotted.
rows.locator: Section 4.2, Phase Transition of Separability; Figure 4a–b
rows.note: The text says validation loss and accuracy suggest separation fails for perr≥2/3. The corruption sweep is on Geo MNIST and does not report training classification error.
rows.check: Figure 4 reports validation outcomes on corrupted Geo MNIST. Its stated failure of separation at corruption ratios at least 2/3 does not establish failure to fit corrupted training labels, and therefore cannot be marked absent for V1.
